root_cause: The `conversation` computed has no memoization; every reactive mutation on any message field (including per-token `content +=`) re-runs the entire 660-line transform: walks every message, JSON.stringify of _rawApiMsg, dangling tool_use filtering, pair validation, consecutive-user dedup.
impact: Every Claude Code-style multi-turn session. Per token in a 100-message session: ~100 JSON.stringify calls on _rawApiMsg blocks + 4× O(n) passes. Hits main thread on every SSE chunk.
fix_sketch: Compute conversation only when messages are added/removed (version counter), not when content mutates. Or store per-message token estimate alongside the message and update incrementally; cache the assembled Anthropic payload by messages-version.
verification: pprof CPU on aiStore.conversation during a 50-turn Claude session; bench a session with `performance.mark` around computed eval.

root_cause: `addMessage` wraps every message in `reactive({ ...msg })` and `_rawApiMsg` is a deep-tracked reactive value. Per-token mutation of `content` invalidates ALL dependents of every message proxy in the dep graph.
impact: All AI sessions. Per-token Vue dep-graph invalidation. With 200 messages in a long session, deep proxies × reactive arrays (tool_calls, _rawApiMsg blocks) inflates the dep graph substantially.
fix_sketch: Use `shallowReactive` for the message wrapper and `markRaw(msg._rawApiMsg)` (it's only mutated by the LLM, never bound UI-side). Buffer streamed text in a non-reactive string assembled at flush time.
verification: Repro: open DevTools Performance recording during a 5K-token response; observe script-time per token.

root_cause: `anthropic-beta: prompt-caching-2024-07-31` header is set, but the request body never has `cache_control: {type:"ephemeral"}` breakpoints on system / tools / last few messages. Static system prompt (~2KB) + tool definitions (~1KB) re-sent and re-billed every turn.
impact: Every multi-turn Claude session. ~3KB wasted tokens + extra latency per turn. Across a 20-turn session that's 60KB of redundant input tokens, plus no cache-hit savings.
fix_sketch: On chatCompletionAnthropic: insert cache_control breakpoint on `system` and on `tools` array. Optionally on the last 3-5 messages for incremental cache hits.
verification: Inspect request body in Wails dev tools; compare cached vs uncached token counts in Anthropic dashboard.

root_cause: `doSave()` is called synchronously on every `addMessage` / `addSkillCard` / `addCommandCard` / `clearMessages`, marshaling and crossing the Wails bridge with the entire conversation history (including JSON.stringify of every `_rawApiMsg`).
evidence:
// aiStore.ts:419  await SaveAISessions(data as any)
// aiStore.ts:276, 296, 315, 327, 514  doSave() called from each mutator + after each chat turn
impact: Every message add. Long sessions push multi-MB per save across the Wails bridge. CPU + bridge cost is paid per token (every tool result adds a message → triggers doSave).
fix_sketch: Debounce doSave (e.g., 500ms trailing); only persist on explicit save / session switch / window blur. Snapshot delta (only the changed session), not the whole array.
verification: Bridge trace of SaveAISessions calls during a 5-turn session; confirm ≤2 calls instead of dozens.

root_cause: Error-path response body reads use unbounded `io.ReadAll(res.Body)` with no size cap. A hostile or buggy upstream returning a multi-GB error body can OOM the Go process.
impact: Any non-200 response from LLM upstream. Currently unlikely in practice but trivial to fix and the cost is unbounded.
fix_sketch: Cap to 64KB: `body, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(res.Body, 64*1024))`.
verification: pprof alloc on a synthetic upstream returning a 100MB 500 error body.

root_cause: Every SSE `data:` line is fully `json.Unmarshal`-ed into a fresh `map[string]interface{}` allocation. Anthropic emits ~1 event per token for content_block_delta; a 2K-token response = 2K map allocations, ~99% of fields discarded immediately.
impact: Per-token allocation pressure on the streaming hot path. Compounds with string-concat accumulator in F-307.
fix_sketch: Define typed structs (MessageStart, ContentBlockDelta with embedded delta, etc.) and decode into them. Use `json.RawMessage` and field-switch on `type` for the small set of event shapes actually handled.
verification: pprof allocs during a streamed 5K-token response.

root_cause: Text delta accumulation uses `currentBlock["text"].(string) + text` (string concat) per token. O(n²) for long responses plus every concat allocates a new string.
impact: Long Claude responses (multi-KB). Allocator pressure and GC churn during streaming.
fix_sketch: Build a `bytes.Buffer` per block; flush to string at content_block_stop / message_stop.
verification: pprof allocs during a 10K-token stream; compare n² vs n.

root_cause: `chatCancel` is a single `context.CancelFunc` field with `chatCancelMu` protecting it. When two `ChatCompletion` calls overlap (retry storm, quick user re-trigger), call A's defer nils out `chatCancel` while call B is still in flight; `CancelChatStream` then becomes a no-op for B.
impact: Stuck stream during retry storms or rapid user re-trigger; observed rarely but high-cost when it happens (request runs to natural completion despite user Stop).
fix_sketch: Use atomic.Pointer[CancelFunc] and only nil the slot if it still points to your own cancel. Or refuse new chat while one is active (serialize at the front door).
verification: Repro: trigger 2 ChatCompletion calls back-to-back; confirm CancelChatStream cancels both.

root_cause: Each `ChatCompletion` builds `client := &http.Client{Timeout: 0}` with default Transport. No `MaxIdleConnsPerHost`, no `IdleConnTimeout`. Every call (and every retry attempt) opens fresh TCP+TLS connections to api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com.
impact: Higher per-request latency (~100-200ms extra per call for TLS handshake) and wasted sockets. Compounds with retry storms.
fix_sketch: Promote a shared `*http.Transport` to the App struct with `MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 4`, `IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second`, `TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second`. Reuse across all LLM calls.
verification: netstat during a chat session; confirm ≤4 idle connections to LLM host.

root_cause: `estimateMessageTokens` does `JSON.stringify(msg._rawApiMsg)` on every message, every time the conversation computed re-evaluates (which is per-token per F-301). For a 100-message session this is 100 redundant JSON stringifies per token.
evidence: // aiStore.ts:45  total += estimateTokens(JSON.stringify(msg._rawApiMsg))
impact: Long sessions, per token. Pure CPU waste — the serialized form never changes for a given `_rawApiMsg`.
fix_sketch: Cache `msg._tokenEstimate` at addMessage time (after JSON.stringify runs once). Track a running total on the conversation computed and decrement/increment on add/remove.
verification: pprof CPU on `stringify` op during a 100-message session.

root_cause: `activeAssistantMsg.content += data.text` is a deep-reactive mutation per SSE token that triggers the entire AISidebar render chain. With high-throughput models (Claude 100+ tok/s, GPT-4o), this is 100+ Vue re-renders per second on the main thread.
impact: Every streaming AI response; visible jank during fast models on lower-end machines.
fix_sketch: Buffer tokens into a non-reactive string; flush to `activeAssistantMsg.content` via `requestAnimationFrame` (16ms cadence). Use `shallowRef` for the displayed text so token appends don't churn the dep graph.
verification: Repro: stream a 5K-token Claude response, observe Chrome Performance recording; aim for ≤60 renders/sec instead of N-tokens/sec.

root_cause: Tool result blobs (execute_command output, capture_terminal screen, use_skill manifest) stored verbatim in `m.content`. A 200-line × 2KB capture_terminal = 400KB retained. The conversation computed (F-301) walks all retained blobs every turn.
impact: Every multi-turn session with tool output > a few KB. Memory grows linearly with total tool-result bytes; per-turn compute grows too.
fix_sketch: Cap tool result blobs at write time (e.g., head+tail truncation, or store large blobs to disk and reference by path/id in the message).
verification: Memory snapshot after a 20-turn Claude Code session that cat'd large files.

root_cause: `conversation` makes multiple linear passes over the message array: build kept (with token-budget break), strip leading tool messages, collect resolved tool_use IDs, second loop filtering, third loop for pair validation, fourth for consecutive-user dedup. O(4n + n·estimateMessageTokens) per chat call.
impact: Per-turn latency before the request is even issued. For 200 messages this is multiple ms of pure JS.
fix_sketch: Single forward pass that validates pairings, deduplicates, and emits output in one loop. Build the `resolvedIds` Set lazily from the same pass.
verification: Bench with console.time around chat() call on a 200-message session.

root_cause: `doSave` materializes a full snapshot via `sessions.value.map(...)` on every call (every message add). For a 200-message session with 4KB `_rawApiMsg` each, that's ~800KB allocated per save + bridged across to Go.
impact: Per message add (couples with F-304). Heavy GC + bridge traffic.
fix_sketch: Diff-based save (only the mutated session). Debounce to coalesce bursts. Pre-stringify `_rawApiMsg` once at `addMessage` so the JSON form is cached.
verification: Bridge traces + heap snapshot during a 20-turn session.

root_cause: Module-level `activeTokenUnsubscribe` / `activeAssistantMsg` shared across runAgent calls. Re-entrant paths (approveTool → runAgent; rejectTool/answerQuestion/dismissQuestion setTimeout→runAgent at lines 1056, 1082, 1099) call `registerTokenListener` which cancels the prior listener, but if an early-return path bypassed `cleanupStreamListeners`, the previous `activeAssistantMsg` may be replaced mid-stream without releasing reactive refs.
impact: Rare re-entry paths; possible Vue reactive proxy leak (per F-302 amplifies this).
fix_sketch: Make `activeTokenUnsubscribe` / `activeAssistantMsg` a single pair guarded by a version counter; ensure cleanupStreamListeners runs on every return path. Or fold re-entry into a single dispatcher.
verification: Repro: approveTool while streaming; inspect Vue DevTools for orphaned reactive proxies.

root_cause: `loadSessionsFromBackend` eagerly `JSON.parse`s `_rawApiMsg` for every message in every saved session at app startup. For 15 sessions × 200 messages, that's 3000 JSON parses; parsed object trees held in memory even for sessions that won't be opened in this session.
evidence:
// aiStore.ts:147
_rawApiMsg: m._rawApiMsg ? JSON.parse(m._rawApiMsg) : undefined,
impact: App startup with a large AI history. Holds multi-MB of parsed object trees in memory.
fix_sketch: Keep `_rawApiMsg` as JSON string; only parse on session switch (when the messages become reactive and may be sent to the API). Or persist as JSON-encoded blob per session and parse on demand.
verification: Memory snapshot before/after loadSessionsFromBackend on a history with 2000 messages.

root_cause: `resolveActiveSession` spreads `panelStore.panels` Map into an Array and runs two `.find` passes (exact title + suffix match) for every command call. O(n) per call.
impact: High panel count (>10). Linear scan per command.
fix_sketch: Maintain a title→panelId index alongside the Map, updated on panelStore mutations. O(1) lookup.
verification: Micro-bench with 50 panels.

root_cause: No background-lifecycle pause for the AI stream. CancelChatStream is only invoked on explicit user Stop. When the app goes to background mid-stream, the LLM stream continues at full speed, the Go-side SSE scanner keeps allocating, EventsEmit keeps crossing the Wails bridge, and Pinia reactivity keeps mutating — paying full idle cost while the user can't see anything. (Compounds with the app-wide App-Nap concern.)
impact: Every streaming AI session running while the app is backgrounded — user can't see UI but app keeps burning CPU/allocations/network.
fix_sketch: Wire `document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', ...)` to call `CancelChatStream` (and pause `doSave` debounce) when `document.hidden`. Optionally resume on visible. On macOS, register an `applicationDidResignActive` hook to throttle further.
verification: Repro: start a 5K-token stream, background the app, observe CPU with Activity Monitor.

root_cause: Request body is `JSON.stringify`-ed once but uses a flat object with the full `AVAILABLE_TOOLS` array (constant ~6KB) and the system prompt + entire conversation embedded every call. There's no template caching of the static prefix (system+tools) — even though they are invariant across all turns of a session.
impact: Couples with F-303 (no cache_control) — full tokens billed for the static prefix every turn. Per-turn latency: 1-2ms JSON.stringify on a 6KB tools array.
fix_sketch: Cache the JSON-serialized `system+tools` prefix at session-start; concatenate with the dynamic `messages` only at send time. Add `cache_control` breakpoints (paired with F-303).
verification: Inspect request body; Anthropic dashboard cached-vs-uncached token count.

root_cause: Every SSE event triggers a `runtime.EventsEmit` carrying a freshly built `map[string]interface{}` payload (ai:block_start / ai:token / ai:input_json_delta / ai:content_block_stop / ai:done). These all cross the Wails bridge to the frontend, getting JSON-marshaled on the Go side and JS-cloned on the WebKit side. Per-token `ai:token` is the worst: a text-only delta plus the index crosses the bridge for every token of every response.
impact: Per-token bridge crossing. With F-302/F-311 the frontend then triggers a deep-reactive mutation on the received data, amplifying the cost. Compounds in long responses.
fix_sketch: Coalesce consecutive `ai:token` events in Go (e.g., 16ms flush window) before crossing the bridge. Or use a single WebSocket-like channel that flushes per animation frame. Drop unused fields from the event payload.
verification: Bridge traffic count during a 5K-token stream; aim for ≤60 token-events/sec.
